neighbours.label: the '1' in a complement expression '1 - p' / '(1 - x)' in a formula
fire: The probability of failure is simply 1 - p when success has probability p.
Multiply the variance by (1 - r) to get the adjusted value.
The logit transform is log(p / (1 - p)) for each estimate.
With a discount factor d, each step keeps 1 - d of the old value.
The binomial variance equals n * p * (1 - p) for the sample.
If a fraction f is lost, the remaining mass is (1 - f) times the start.
The survival curve follows S(t) = (1 - q)^t in this model.
Set the weight to 1 - alpha so that both terms sum to one.
quiet: The probability of success is simply p when each trial is independent.
Multiply the variance by r squared to get the adjusted value.
The log transform is log(p) for each estimate.
With a growth factor g, each step multiplies the old value by g.
The binomial mean equals n * p for the sample.
If a fraction f is lost, the lost mass is f times the start.
The growth curve follows G(t) = q^t in this model.
Set the weight to alpha so that the first term dominates.

notes: Card: no dominant token; top is 'log[(p/(1 - p)]', others are numeric literals in code and tables. Probe: 'p/(1 - p)' 0.94; code assignments '= 0' ~0.05. Near misses keep formulas about p without a '1 -' complement. Opposite pole: numeric literals in arithmetic code.
